name: Coffin-Siris Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Coffin-Siris Syndrome

criteria.description: Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Hypoplasia or aplasia of the fifth digit nails or distal phalanges
Coarse facial features including thick eyebrows, wide nasal bridge, and thick lips
Pathogenic mutation in genes encoding the BAF chromatin remodeling complex
Postnatal growth retardation or short stature
Early feeding difficulties or failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of developmental delay, fifth-digit nail hypoplasia, and distinctive facial features; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in ARID1B and other BAF complex genes is recommended to confirm diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplasia or aplasia of fifth digit nails

pathognomonic.notes: Includes thick eyebrows, wide nasal bridge, thick lips

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible hypothyroidism on thyroid panel
Immunological workup may reveal mild immunodeficiency
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific findings such as delayed myelination
Skeletal X-rays reveal hypoplasia of distal phalanges of fifth digits
genetic: Pathogenic variants in ARID1B gene (most common)
Mutations in other BAF complex genes including SMARCA4, SMARCB1, SMARCE1
other: Clinical evaluation reveals characteristic facial gestalt and fifth digit abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Severe feeding difficulties and failure to thrive

redFlags: Severe global developmental delay with absent speech
Hypoplasia or aplasia of fifth digit nails
Distinctive coarse facial features with thick eyebrows and wide nasal bridge
references: Tsurusaki Y, et al. Mutations affecting components of the SWI/SNF complex cause Coffin-Siris syndrome. Nat Genet. 2012.
Santen GW, et al. Coffin-Siris syndrome and the BAF complex: genotype-phenotype study in 63 patients. Hum Mutat. 2013.
Hoyer J, et al. Haploinsufficiency of ARID1B, a member of the SWI/SNF-A chromatin-remodeling complex, is a frequent cause of intellectual disability. Am J Hum Genet. 2012.
